cards.title: Where did agents say they were confused?
cards.recipe: Search agent-authored text for a curated family of uncertainty phrases; group by phrase and repository; count distinct conversations as well as occurrences.
cards.preview: One highlighted excerpt above a short phrase ranking.
cards.eligibility: At least one exact match in agent text; exclude quoted user text and injected instructions where provenance permits.
cards.destination: Matched messages with surrounding turns and their conversations.
cards.exploration_value: Finds concrete moments worth clarifying in future instructions.
cards.blocked_on_pharos: Add a canonical messages or phrase-match relation with role, message time, match family, source span and parent conversation.
cards.calculation_gap: Library find returns workspace membership; it cannot apply agent role and rolling time to the actual matched message through QueryState.
cards.performance_note: Use FTS before grouping; a recently active workspace can contain an old match and is not evidence of a recent phrase.

capacity_audit.reason: Library find returns workspace membership; it cannot apply agent role and rolling time to the actual matched message through QueryState.

cards.title: What did I have to correct?
cards.recipe: Search human-authored messages for explicit corrections such as 'you misunderstood' and 'not what I asked'; rank recurring literal phrases and show context.
cards.preview: User correction paired with the immediately preceding agent response.
cards.eligibility: At least one correction phrase; label phrase matches rather than proven misunderstandings.
cards.destination: Correction messages and preceding agent turns.
cards.exploration_value: Makes repeated steering visible without claiming to read the user's mood.
cards.blocked_on_pharos: Expose correction phrase families and bounded neighbor-message hydration; preserve genuine human authorship.
cards.calculation_gap: writing_messages can filter literal human corrections by sent_at; it cannot return the paired preceding agent response as a normal metric result.
cards.performance_note: Date-bounded LIKE is viable for a small window but an indexed message search route is better at archive scale.

capacity_audit.reason: writing_messages can filter literal human corrections by sent_at; it cannot return the paired preceding agent response as a normal metric result.

cards.title: What instructions am I repeating?
cards.recipe: Normalize repeated human-authored instruction spans; cluster exact or near-exact repetitions across distinct conversations; separate templates and re-sent text.
cards.preview: Repeated sentence with a row of conversation marks.
cards.eligibility: A repeated span in at least three distinct conversations; confirm it is instruction text before naming it a rule.
cards.destination: Repeated spans grouped by conversation and repository.
cards.exploration_value: Suggests candidates for reusable instructions or skills.
cards.blocked_on_pharos: Exact human-message repeats now require three distinct conversations. Instruction spans, normalization and near-duplicate families still need an extractor.
cards.calculation_gap: Exact human-message repeats now require three distinct conversations. Instruction spans, normalization and near-duplicate families still need an extractor.
cards.performance_note: Materialize cluster memberships and support counts; do not normalize every transcript on reload.

capacity_audit.reason: Exact human-message repeats now require three distinct conversations. Instruction spans, normalization and near-duplicate families still need an extractor.

cards.title: How many exchanges does a task take?
cards.recipe: For each canonical conversation count genuine human-to-agent exchanges; aggregate median, upper quartile and distribution by repository and task family when available.
cards.preview: Compact histogram with median marker; a small repository comparison.
cards.eligibility: Several complete conversations with human participation; exclude automated launch messages and report unfinished sessions separately.
cards.destination: Conversation-level exchange counts and transcripts.
cards.exploration_value: Reveals the shape of collaboration rather than just message volume.
cards.blocked_on_pharos: Windowed human-message counts and their conversation-level histogram now execute. Genuine exchange boundaries, complete task lifetimes, completion coverage and task labels remain absent.
cards.calculation_gap: Windowed human-message counts and their conversation-level histogram now execute. Genuine exchange boundaries, complete task lifetimes, completion coverage and task labels remain absent.
cards.performance_note: Distributions need per-conversation rows; alternatively group filtered message facts, then reduce the groups in a second stage.

capacity_audit.reason: Windowed human-message counts and their conversation-level histogram now execute. Genuine exchange boundaries, complete task lifetimes, completion coverage and task labels remain absent.

cards.title: Where do conversations keep circling back?
cards.recipe: Classify repeated problem statements and alternating proposed fixes within each conversation; rank loops by number of returns and preserve supporting excerpts.
cards.preview: A three-step loop with repeated text highlighted.
cards.eligibility: Multiple evidenced returns to the same problem; similarity alone does not prove lack of progress.
cards.destination: Candidate loops with intervening turns and tool results.
cards.exploration_value: Finds topics whose explanation or diagnosis may need improvement.
cards.blocked_on_pharos: Materialize evidence-backed loop episodes with repeated-topic links and intervening events.
cards.calculation_gap: No current metric or forthcoming scalar formula identifies semantic return-to-problem loops.
cards.performance_note: Query ranked episode facts; neither a histogram nor a repeated phrase alone establishes a loop.

capacity_audit.reason: No current metric or forthcoming scalar formula identifies semantic return-to-problem loops.

cards.title: When do agents ask me to do their work?
cards.recipe: Classify agent requests for user action; distinguish useful decisions from requests to run commands, copy outputs or perform available routine actions.
cards.preview: Request excerpt with categories such as decision, command and information.
cards.eligibility: At least one classified request; capability availability requires evidence before calling a request avoidable.
cards.destination: Requests and the capabilities available in that session.
cards.exploration_value: Surfaces opportunities to reduce manual handoffs.
cards.blocked_on_pharos: Extract agent requests, action type and capability evidence; retain uncertainty about whether the action was avoidable.
cards.calculation_gap: Phrase filters can find candidate requests, but available capabilities and avoidable handoffs are not classified rows.
cards.performance_note: Run extraction at indexing and filter its annotations; avoid expensive classification during card eligibility checks.

capacity_audit.reason: Phrase filters can find candidate requests, but available capabilities and avoidable handoffs are not classified rows.

cards.title: Which conversations end with explicit positive feedback?
cards.recipe: Find human-authored approval or thanks phrases; count distinct conversations and distinguish task acceptance from politeness through context.
cards.preview: Short user quote with a strip of linked conversations.
cards.eligibility: At least one positive-feedback match; do not label it objective correctness.
cards.destination: Feedback messages and the preceding result.
cards.exploration_value: Balances friction cards with examples worth repeating.
cards.blocked_on_pharos: Literal positive-feedback candidates now execute with representative messages. Final-message position, acceptance versus politeness, and predecessor pairing remain unclassified.
cards.calculation_gap: Literal positive-feedback candidates now execute with representative messages. Final-message position, acceptance versus politeness, and predecessor pairing remain unclassified.
cards.performance_note: Indexed literal candidates are inexpensive; classification can be cached by message hash and extractor version.

capacity_audit.reason: Literal positive-feedback candidates now execute with representative messages. Final-message position, acceptance versus politeness, and predecessor pairing remain unclassified.

cards.title: Where did I change the goal midway?
cards.recipe: Identify explicit changes in requirements after work started; record the change point and summarize the original and revised request.
cards.preview: Two contrasting request fragments connected by a small pivot arrow.
cards.eligibility: An evidenced scope change; distinguish a changed goal from clarification of the same goal.
cards.destination: Before-and-after request messages and intervening work.
cards.exploration_value: Helps users understand what kinds of tasks need early alignment.
cards.blocked_on_pharos: Extract explicit scope changes and link original and revised requests to canonical work.
cards.calculation_gap: The archive contains requests in order, but a goal-change relation and before/after pair do not exist.
cards.performance_note: Index changes once; Query Table can already filter and group the resulting annotations.

capacity_audit.reason: The archive contains requests in order, but a goal-change relation and before/after pair do not exist.

cards.title: Which tool calls fail most often?
cards.recipe: Group calls by tool, program, subcommand or MCP method; compute failure count and failures divided by observed calls; rank both volume and rate.
cards.preview: Three labeled bars with failed and total counts.
cards.eligibility: Error-bearing groups with usable denominators; preserve no-result and interrupted statuses separately.
cards.destination: Failed calls plus the complete call population for each group.
cards.exploration_value: Reveals tool reliability in a way users can immediately investigate.
cards.current_preview: Error volume by tool. Recorded error calls started in the last 30 days, split by tool. Tool failure rates. Error calls divided by all calls started in the last 30 days; tools with ten or more calls. Repository failure rates. Error calls divided by all calls started in the last 30 days; repositories with ten or more calls. Tool call mix. Recorded calls started in the last 30 days, split by tool. Calls per conversation. Tool calls per recorded agent conversation over the last 30 days; repositories with three or more conversations.
cards.blocked_on_pharos: Source-population failure rates and minimum group support now execute before ranking. Bounded failed-call examples and source/timing completeness remain host evidence work.
cards.calculation_gap: Source-population failure rates and minimum group support now execute before ranking. Bounded failed-call examples and source/timing completeness remain host evidence work.
cards.performance_note: SUM(error_count)/SUM(call_count) is enabled by v2; retain cube routing and minimum exposure before top-K.

capacity_audit.reason: Source-population failure rates and minimum group support now execute before ranking. Bounded failed-call examples and source/timing completeness remain host evidence work.

cards.title: Which error keeps coming back?
cards.recipe: Group failed calls by normalized error signature; count distinct conversations and repositories alongside total failures.
cards.preview: A prominent error fragment with a repository dot strip.
cards.eligibility: A repeated signature in more than one call or conversation; exclude volatile IDs and paths from grouping.
cards.destination: All calls with the selected signature and their raw results.
cards.exploration_value: Finds one fix that may benefit many sessions.
cards.current_preview: Recurring error signatures. Diagnostic signatures on at least two error calls started in the last 30 days, with conversation reach. Errors across repositories. Signatures shared by at least two named repositories over the last 30 days, ranked by repository reach. Failures per conversation. Error calls per affected agent conversation over the last 30 days; tools with three or more affected conversations.
cards.blocked_on_pharos: Hydrate bounded raw error examples; preserve signature normalization and mirror exclusion.
cards.calculation_gap: Distinct reach is executable; bounded raw error hydration remains host work.
cards.performance_note: Group a bounded failed-call population; distinct conversation/repository counts may bypass sum-only summaries.

capacity_audit.reason: Distinct reach is executable; bounded raw error hydration remains host work.

cards.title: What do agents do after a failure?
cards.recipe: Sequence calls after comparable failures; categorize unchanged retry, changed arguments, different tool and user intervention; measure next observed outcome.
cards.preview: Branching recovery path with counts on each branch.
cards.eligibility: Enough failure episodes with retained follow-up calls; unresolved tails remain unknown.
cards.destination: Failure episodes with their next calls and results.
cards.exploration_value: Exposes recovery strategies worth copying or improving.
cards.blocked_on_pharos: Expose stream identity, stable event order, normalized actions and recovery episode facts.
cards.calculation_gap: Ordered calls exist in storage, but the metric contract cannot select the next relevant call or recovery episode.
cards.performance_note: Precompute episodes incrementally or use bounded ordered partitions; success tails and unfinished episodes remain explicit.

capacity_audit.reason: Ordered calls exist in storage, but the metric contract cannot select the next relevant call or recovery episode.

cards.title: Where do unchanged retries pile up?
cards.recipe: Normalize call arguments within each stream; find repeated equivalent failing calls before meaningful changes; aggregate excess attempts and their attributed cost.
cards.preview: Repeated command tiles with the changed attempt emphasized.
cards.eligibility: At least one repeated failure sequence; exclude polling, intentional sampling and status checks.
cards.destination: Retry sequences and argument differences.
cards.exploration_value: Makes repetitive dead ends obvious.
cards.blocked_on_pharos: Exact recurring failed build/test/package commands now execute. They are not adjacent retries: normalized argument identity, stream order, intentional repetition exclusions and episode attribution remain absent.
cards.calculation_gap: Exact recurring failed build/test/package commands now execute. They are not adjacent retries: normalized argument identity, stream order, intentional repetition exclusions and episode attribution remain absent.
cards.performance_note: Use stream/order indexes and cached episode facts, not a Cartesian self-join over the tool ledger. October 14 real-library check: the new primary-URL and exact repeated-command previews can exceed the 15-second deadline at 90 days. Defaults use 7/30 days; longer windows remain available to open directly.

capacity_audit.reason: Exact recurring failed build/test/package commands now execute. They are not adjacent retries: normalized argument identity, stream order, intentional repetition exclusions and episode attribution remain absent.

cards.title: Which calls consume the most recorded waiting time?
cards.recipe: Rank commands by total measured duration and show median and upper percentile where per-call timing is available; split reported from timestamp-derived durations.
cards.preview: Horizontal duration bars with a marked long tail.
cards.eligibility: Sufficient timed calls; show timing coverage and do not describe timestamp gaps as pure tool runtime.
cards.destination: Timed calls with duration source and slow examples.
cards.exploration_value: Finds test suites, builds or requests that dominate recorded elapsed time.
cards.current_preview: Command duration spread. Positive recorded call durations in the last 30 days, by command and timing source; three-call minimum.
cards.blocked_on_pharos: Grouped totals, scalar MEDIAN and exact duration distributions now execute. Arbitrary scalar p95 and fuller timing-coverage comparisons remain unavailable.
cards.calculation_gap: Grouped totals, scalar MEDIAN and exact duration distributions now execute. Arbitrary scalar p95 and fuller timing-coverage comparisons remain unavailable.
cards.performance_note: Exact quartiles/p95 scan or sort call samples; daily min/max/sum cannot reconstruct percentiles.

capacity_audit.reason: Grouped totals, scalar MEDIAN and exact duration distributions now execute. Arbitrary scalar p95 and fuller timing-coverage comparisons remain unavailable.

cards.title: What starts failing after a change?
cards.recipe: Compare error signatures and failure rates before and after an observed harness, tool configuration or project change; join by stable dimensions and exposure.
cards.preview: Before-and-after bars with a change marker.
cards.eligibility: Both periods have calls and comparable coverage; a change marker is association, not proof of cause.
cards.destination: Calls and recorded changes in the compared periods.
cards.exploration_value: Gives users a concrete lead when a workflow deteriorates.
cards.blocked_on_pharos: Expose tool/harness/project change events and compatible exposures around each anchor.
cards.calculation_gap: Failure counts exist but the dated configuration-change anchors and aligned populations are not a generic query source.
cards.performance_note: Reuse indexed bounded period scans or event-relative facts; preserve versions and avoid automatic causal claims.

capacity_audit.reason: Failure counts exist but the dated configuration-change anchors and aligned populations are not a generic query source.

cards.title: Where do edits fail to apply?
cards.recipe: Filter edit-related file_not_read, edit_no_match, file_not_found and related errors; group by file, repository and edit mechanism.
cards.preview: File names beside small stacked error marks.
cards.eligibility: At least one edit-related failure with a resolved path or known tool.
cards.destination: Failed edits and the reads or changes preceding them.
cards.exploration_value: Finds stale context and fragile editing patterns.
cards.current_preview: Failed edit paths. Error-marked edit calls started in the last 30 days, grouped by repository and mapped relative path.
cards.blocked_on_pharos: Hydrate failed-call details and preceding reads for sequence covers.
cards.calculation_gap: Grouped measures execute now; the original sequence/excerpt cover still needs parent-call hydration.
cards.performance_note: Timestamp and error/path indexes are useful; command-text predicates may require trigram filtering or a fallback scan.

capacity_audit.reason: Grouped measures execute now; the original sequence/excerpt cover still needs parent-call hydration.

cards.title: Which failures spread across repositories?
cards.recipe: For each error signature compute repository breadth, first and recent occurrence, and within-repository rates; rank errors common across otherwise different projects.
cards.preview: Small repository-by-error matrix.
cards.eligibility: A signature appears in at least two repositories with usable call populations.
cards.destination: Shared signatures split by repository and tool version when known.
cards.exploration_value: Distinguishes a shared environment problem from a local project issue.
cards.current_preview: Repository error hotspots. Repository/signature pairs ranked by recorded error calls started in the last 30 days; counts, not rates.
cards.blocked_on_pharos: Supply compatible repository call exposures and version/source coverage; original heatmap requires a renderer.
cards.calculation_gap: Recorded counts and reach are available; exposure-normalized comparison and native heatmaps remain deferred.
cards.performance_note: Distinct breadth plus counts can be computed from bounded calls; apply multi-repository eligibility before group limiting.

capacity_audit.reason: Recorded counts and reach are available; exposure-normalized comparison and native heatmaps remain deferred.

cards.title: Which outputs keep being paid for?
cards.recipe: Rank tool results by attributed context-carried tokens and API-equivalent context cost; retain the originating result and number of later requests.
cards.preview: One output source feeding repeated request marks.
cards.eligibility: Calls with retained results and usable carriage estimates; show estimation provenance.
cards.destination: Results ranked by context carried and attributed cost.
cards.exploration_value: Explains why a small early result can matter more than a large late one.
cards.blocked_on_pharos: Persist or SQL-bind versioned per-call pricing components with provenance before sorting/aggregating.
cards.calculation_gap: carried_tokens and carried_requests are globally queryable now; per-call context cost is added only after page fetch.
cards.performance_note: Token ranking is indexable already; accurate dollar ranking needs a queryable priced fact rather than enrichment of a selected page.

capacity_audit.reason: carried_tokens and carried_requests are globally queryable now; per-call context cost is added only after page fetch.

cards.title: What floods the context window?
cards.recipe: Rank retained tool results by added tokens or bytes; group by command and include truncation and measured-versus-estimated provenance.
cards.preview: A few output blocks sized by added tokens, with a clipped-output marker.
cards.eligibility: At least one unusually large result relative to the user's own call distribution.
cards.destination: Large tool results and their original calls.
cards.exploration_value: Points to narrower searches and quieter commands.
cards.current_preview: Tool context additions. Attributed result tokens from calls started in the last 30 days, split by tool and attribution source. Tool truncation rates. Truncated share of all calls started in the last 30 days, by tool; ten-call minimum. Tool result sizes. Nonempty result sizes for calls started in the last 30 days; three-call minimum per tool/source group.
cards.blocked_on_pharos: Retain token-source provenance and hydrate bounded raw output excerpts.
cards.calculation_gap: Distributions and paired metrics execute now; personal outlier classification is separate analysis.
cards.performance_note: Existing result-token indexes help top rows; exact personalized percentile thresholds need a separate distribution pass.

capacity_audit.reason: Distributions and paired metrics execute now; personal outlier classification is separate analysis.

cards.title: Which files get read again and again?
cards.recipe: Resolve canonical repository paths; count repeated reads within streams and across conversations; separate unchanged content from reads after edits when content identity is available.
cards.preview: File ranking with read marks distributed along a session strip.
cards.eligibility: Repeated resolved-path reads; only call them unchanged when content evidence supports it.
cards.destination: Read events for the selected paths and intervening edits.
cards.exploration_value: Reveals stable context that may be worth packaging or loading differently.
cards.current_preview: Rereads within conversations. Repository paths read at least twice in one recorded conversation during the last 30 days.

capacity_audit.reason: Repeated path counts are available; stream-specific unchanged-content repeats are not.

cards.title: Where do agents search without finding anything?
cards.recipe: Identify explicit empty search results; cluster queries and count subsequent searches before the first retained match; keep valid no-match exit codes distinct from errors.

cards.eligibility: Retained search outputs distinguish empty from missing results.
cards.destination: Search sequences and the successful or unresolved end.
cards.exploration_value: Shows discovery friction that ordinary error counts miss.
cards.current_preview: Pharos empty-search rates. Zero-result share of successful Pharos searches with recorded counts over the last 30 days; ten-call minimum.

cards.calculation_gap: Successful zero-item Pharos MCP search responses now execute; null result counts and error/disabled calls are excluded. General shell/web empty-search outcomes and ordered recovery episodes remain absent.
cards.performance_note: Query stored result-count/episode fields. Zero matches from rg should not be counted as a tool error.

capacity_audit.reason: Successful zero-item Pharos MCP search responses now execute; null result counts and error/disabled calls are excluded. General shell/web empty-search outcomes and ordered recovery episodes remain absent.

cards.title: How long before the first meaningful action?
cards.recipe: Sequence each session from its first request to its first edit, test, decision or other task-appropriate action; show preceding reads and searches.
cards.preview: Session strips with the first selected action marked.
cards.eligibility: Complete event ordering; label first edit or first test literally unless task-specific meaning is classified.
cards.destination: Sessions ordered by time and events before the selected milestone.
cards.exploration_value: Helps inspect whether agents spend too much effort orienting themselves.

capacity_audit.reason: Calls have timestamps, but request-to-first-action milestones and task-appropriate action semantics are not exposed.

cards.title: What happens around compaction?
cards.recipe: Compare events immediately before and after recorded compactions; count repeated reads, renewed searches and explicit re-explanations in matched windows.
cards.preview: Context trace with a compaction notch and repeated events on either side.
cards.eligibility: Recorded compactions with retained neighboring events; do not infer forgotten information merely from a reset.
cards.destination: Compaction episodes and their surrounding transcript windows.
cards.exploration_value: Makes the consequences of context resets inspectable.
cards.blocked_on_pharos: Expose compaction events and linked ordered message/call windows, plus repeat-event facts.

capacity_audit.reason: Library compaction_count can select affected work but does not locate compactions or surrounding rereads.

cards.title: Which instructions are loaded most heavily?
cards.recipe: Group retained skill or instruction bodies by content bytes and distinct streams; show known context attribution only when the parent event supports it.

cards.eligibility: Retained instruction bodies with size evidence; avoid inventing file size or charging a workflow to a skill load.
cards.destination: Instruction loading evidence and retained bodies.
cards.exploration_value: Reveals what occupies context before task work begins.

cards.calculation_gap: Retained successful skill-load body bytes are queryable and separated by evidence type. Broader instruction bodies, exact content identity and deduplicated context attribution remain absent.

capacity_audit.reason: Retained successful skill-load body bytes are queryable and separated by evidence type. Broader instruction bodies, exact content identity and deduplicated context attribution remain absent.

cards.title: What do agents look at most?
cards.recipe: Combine resolved file reads, search queries, reached domains and skill loads; rank by distinct sessions and show concentration by repository.
cards.preview: A compact attention map of paths and sources.
cards.eligibility: Known event attribution; keep reads, searches and loads as distinguishable event types.
cards.destination: The ranked sources and every supporting access event.
cards.exploration_value: Gives users a surprisingly concrete portrait of agent attention.
cards.current_preview: Most-read repository paths. Read calls started in the last 30 days per repository path, with distinct recorded conversation counts.
cards.blocked_on_pharos: Normalize file reads, searches, URL visits and skill loads with source kind and canonical stream/session IDs.
cards.calculation_gap: Tool-call and skill tables each cover some attention events, but there is no unified typed source-event relation.
cards.performance_note: A prepared UNION-style host dataset can support ordinary grouping; distinct session counts prevent large outputs from dominating every ranking.

capacity_audit.reason: Tool-call and skill tables each cover some attention events, but there is no unified typed source-event relation.

cards.title: Which tests fail repeatedly?
cards.recipe: Group observed test failures by normalized test or failure signature and command; include failure markers even when shell status was successful.
cards.preview: Test name and a red-green run strip.
cards.eligibility: Retained test-failure evidence; test identifiers require extraction from output.
cards.destination: Test calls with failure output and later passes when present.
cards.exploration_value: Finds recurring verification trouble that generic command status can hide.
cards.current_preview: Reported test failures. Calls with a recorded test-failure signal started in the last 30 days, grouped by repository and command.

cards.title: Which tests eventually turn green?
cards.recipe: Link comparable test runs within each stream; find failure-to-pass sequences and count intervening edits or attempts.
cards.preview: A failing run crossing into a passing run with edit ticks between.
cards.eligibility: Explicit comparable failure and pass evidence; a zero exit from an unrelated command is insufficient.
cards.destination: Recovery episodes with test identity, edits and results.
cards.exploration_value: Highlights successful debugging paths worth learning from.

cards.title: Where are edits followed by verification?
cards.recipe: Within each work stream connect edit events to later related test, build or lint commands; aggregate coverage by repository and task family.
cards.preview: File or repository grid with verified, unobserved and unknown cells.
cards.eligibility: Retained edits and verification events; no retained test means no observed verification, not proof none occurred.
cards.destination: Edited work grouped by observed verification evidence.

cards.blocked_on_pharos: Derive edit-to-check links and coverage states, with a conservative path/test relevance mapping.

cards.title: Which completions have no retained verification?
cards.recipe: Detect explicit agent completion claims and join them to observed checks after the last relevant edit; show claims without supporting retained checks.
cards.preview: Completion excerpt above a small empty check lane.
cards.eligibility: Explicit completion text plus usable event coverage; call it missing retained evidence rather than untested work.

capacity_audit.reason: Completion claims are transcript text, and missing retained checks cannot be inferred from a work outcome label alone.

cards.title: How many edit and test cycles does a fix take?
cards.recipe: Sessionize alternating edits and comparable verification runs; count cycles until an observed pass; show median and distribution per failure family.
cards.preview: Edit-test beads ending in a green mark.
cards.eligibility: Comparable runs with retained ordering; unresolved sequences remain separate.
cards.destination: Cycle histories and grouped cycle counts.
cards.exploration_value: Quantifies iteration without equating fewer cycles with better work.
cards.blocked_on_pharos: Derive comparable edit/test cycle episodes and their observed terminal state.
cards.calculation_gap: No episode/cycle input exists; v2 histogram over calls would show call values, not edit-test cycles per fix.

capacity_audit.reason: No episode/cycle input exists; v2 histogram over calls would show call values, not edit-test cycles per fix.

cards.title: Which checks are skipped after the final change?
cards.recipe: Find completed work where the last relevant check preceded the final relevant edit; distinguish pass-before-edit from check-after-edit.
cards.preview: Timeline with final edit positioned after the last check.
cards.eligibility: Relevant edits and checks plus an observed end state; relevance may require file-to-test mapping or classification.
cards.destination: Final edit and check order for each matched work.

cards.blocked_on_pharos: Derive genuine exchange rounds and action-run facts with comparable prior-window coverage.

cards.title: How much time is tool work versus gaps between events?
cards.recipe: Union overlapping timed tool intervals within each stream; compare with observed session spans and label remaining gaps without assigning them to thinking or human work.
cards.preview: A timeline with timed calls and unclassified gaps.
cards.eligibility: Complete timed intervals and explicit coverage; never sum parallel durations as elapsed wall time.
cards.destination: Timed calls, overlap handling and unclassified intervals.
cards.exploration_value: Helps inspect workflow timing without inventing hidden activity.
cards.blocked_on_pharos: Publish timed intervals, observed spans and coverage at stream grain, or materialize union length and unclassified gaps.
cards.calculation_gap: Per-call timings can be summed but that gives incorrect elapsed time for overlap; session span completeness also varies.
cards.performance_note: Union overlap before computing fractions; open intervals and missing timings remain unknown.

capacity_audit.reason: Per-call timings can be summed but that gives incorrect elapsed time for overlap; session span completeness also varies.

cards.title: Which workflows would I happily repeat?
cards.recipe: Find work with explicit positive acceptance, usable verification, modest human steering and reusable task structure; show each criterion separately.
cards.preview: Starting prompt paired with acceptance evidence and a short workflow trace.
cards.eligibility: Supported acceptance and relevant verification; avoid a single opaque success score.
cards.destination: Candidate workflows with criteria and source passages.
cards.exploration_value: Offers positive examples the user can collect as future starting points.
cards.blocked_on_pharos: Prepare evidence-backed workflow criteria and source passages; preserve separate criteria instead of an opaque success score.
cards.calculation_gap: Work outcomes and writing can provide candidates, but explicit acceptance, relevant verification and reusable structure are not complete joined facts.
cards.performance_note: Query stored criteria at canonical work grain; recommendations and judgments are Pharos product logic.

capacity_audit.reason: Work outcomes and writing can provide candidates, but explicit acceptance, relevant verification and reusable structure are not complete joined facts.

cards.title: Which recoveries are worth learning from?
cards.recipe: Rank failure-to-recovery episodes by recurrence, changed strategy and explicit observed resolution; show the pivotal changed call or instruction.
cards.preview: Failure fragment, pivotal action and observed recovery in three frames.
cards.eligibility: A retained failure and comparable successful follow-up; causal wording needs more than sequence alone.
cards.destination: Complete recovery episodes and their pivotal evidence.
cards.exploration_value: Turns mistakes into a library of useful techniques.
cards.blocked_on_pharos: Publish recurring recovery episodes with resolution evidence and action-difference annotations.
cards.calculation_gap: Raw failures and later calls exist, but linked recovery episodes and the pivotal changed action do not.
cards.performance_note: Rank indexed episode facts by recurrence and useful evidence; don't rerun transcript sequence extraction for every refresh.

capacity_audit.reason: Raw failures and later calls exist, but linked recovery episodes and the pivotal changed action do not.

cards.title: Which improvements stayed improved?
cards.recipe: Join recorded fixes or findings to before-and-after failure exposure; inspect recurrence over successive windows and include confidence or small-sample labels.
cards.preview: A before-and-after rate trace with the fix date.
cards.eligibility: Dated fix and compatible ongoing exposure; absence of recurrence with no exposure is not success.
cards.destination: Fix evidence, relevant failures and observation denominators.
cards.exploration_value: Helps users understand which interventions are holding up.
cards.blocked_on_pharos: Expose fix/measurement and relevant call-population facts with observation coverage.

capacity_audit.reason: Findings rows carry likely savings and verified net savings, so open-finding and result cards are ordinary aggregations; recurrence over successive windows remains deferred.

cards.title: What new kinds of work am I trying?
cards.recipe: Classify requests into task families and compare with the preceding window; show newly observed families with representative requests.
cards.preview: Three request fragments with small first-observed timeline marks.
cards.eligibility: Task-family evidence and enough earlier coverage; do not claim first-ever activity from a short archive.
cards.destination: Work in the newly observed families.

cards.blocked_on_pharos: Materialize versioned task-family labels and representative requests, including multi-label membership semantics.
cards.calculation_gap: Purpose summaries offer text but not a stable task-family taxonomy with prior-window coverage.

capacity_audit.reason: Purpose summaries offer text but not a stable task-family taxonomy with prior-window coverage.

cards.title: What combinations of tools are unusual for me?
cards.recipe: Build ordered workflow motifs within streams; compare recent sequences with the preceding window and surface supported uncommon combinations.
cards.preview: A novel three-tool path with a representative result fragment.
cards.eligibility: A valid recent motif and sufficient prior sequence coverage; novelty is not superiority.
cards.destination: Sessions containing the motif and their outcomes.
cards.exploration_value: Gives the conveyor surprising, concrete discoveries beyond top-N rankings.
cards.blocked_on_pharos: Produce bounded typed workflow motifs and marginal frequencies at stream grain.

capacity_audit.reason: Tool categories can be counted but ordered motifs and personal historical rarity are not fields.

cards.title: What is the playbook for a new repository?
cards.recipe: Detect recently observed repositories and summarize evidenced recurring setup commands, test commands, documentation sources and early obstacles.
cards.preview: A tiny repository map with two real commands and one source.
cards.eligibility: Several retained sessions in a newly observed repository; distinguish common actions from recommended best practice.
cards.destination: The repository's startup work and supporting events.
cards.exploration_value: Turns the user's recent experience into a useful orientation view.
cards.blocked_on_pharos: Build repository orientation facts with actual setup/test/source examples and explicit recently-observed status.

capacity_audit.reason: Repository commands, domains and first observed activity can be selected; an evidenced playbook involves extraction and interpretation.

cards.title: What deserves a reusable instruction or skill?
cards.recipe: Combine repeated human instructions, recurring recovery procedures and reused examples; rank candidate procedures by recurrence and explicit successful use.
cards.preview: Repeated rule plus two short evidenced workflow steps.

cards.destination: Candidate procedures, repeated requests and observed outcomes.
cards.exploration_value: Connects exploration to durable improvements in the user's toolkit.
cards.blocked_on_pharos: Combine instruction/recovery/example annotations into candidate reusable procedures with evidence links.

capacity_audit.reason: Repeated rules, procedures and their explicit successful use are not normalized evidence relations.

cards.title: What would I miss in an average?
cards.recipe: For distributions already supported by the data surface bimodality, a concentrated tail or cohort reversals; show the grouped and ungrouped views together.

query_table_requests.title: Filter evaluated row values before paging
query_table_requests.gap: V3 applies admitted computed source predicates before paging/grouping. Host-produced derived fields still need actual bindings and capabilities.
query_table_requests.proposal: Add capability-gated typed predicates over server-evaluated fields before total counts, page selection and all-matching metrics; retain unsupported clauses with diagnostics.
query_table_requests.performance: Push predicates into the authoritative relation; stable host projections or expression indexes may help measured hot definitions. Page-local filtering is incorrect.
query_table_requests.current_status: V3 applies admitted computed source predicates before paging/grouping. Host-produced derived fields still need actual bindings and capabilities.

query_table_requests.title: Filter grouped results before ranking and limiting
query_table_requests.gap: Row-producing groups expose typed HAVING predicates before ranking/paging; failure rates and repeated-message/skill groups use them.
query_table_requests.proposal: Add validated aggregate-result predicates such as distinct conversations >= 3, observations >= 20, failures > 0 and rate > threshold. Evaluate before result LIMIT and expose final group count.
query_table_requests.performance: Filter before top-K. Client filtering of a capped group list can miss eligible groups and produce incorrect recommendations.
query_table_requests.current_status: Row-producing groups expose typed HAVING predicates before ranking/paging; failure rates and repeated-message/skill groups use them.

query_table_requests.title: Reduce grouped results in a second explicit stage
query_table_requests.gap: A bounded source grouping creates typed rows, then result metrics reduce them. Conversation-writing charts histogram windowed conversation counts.
query_table_requests.proposal: Support a bounded group → typed result relation → project/filter → second reduction pipeline. Example: sum usage per conversation, then histogram those totals by repository. A host-supplied derived dataset remains an alternative.
query_table_requests.performance: Keep both stages on the server and limit stages/group cardinality. Intermediate relation semantics must preserve grain and row lineage.
query_table_requests.current_status: A bounded source grouping creates typed rows, then result metrics reduce them. Conversation-writing charts histogram windowed conversation counts.

query_table_requests.title: Time buckets and aligned period comparisons
query_table_requests.gap: Native relative elapsed operands and IANA timezone calendar buckets execute with one clock through V3. Aligned before/after populations and change anchors still need explicit facts/queries.
query_table_requests.proposal: Expose tested timezone-aware time bucket fields/functions and current/previous or before/after period selection under one evaluation clock. Define gaps, unequal durations, civil versus elapsed time and rate denominators.
query_table_requests.performance: Lower relative ranges to indexed timestamp bounds; reuse period scans and existing daily facts. A formatting timezone does not change grouping timezone.
query_table_requests.current_status: Native relative elapsed operands and IANA timezone calendar buckets execute with one clock through V3. Aligned before/after populations and change anchors still need explicit facts/queries.

query_table_requests.title: Named measures and shared reductions at one grain
query_table_requests.gap: V3 produces named summaries at one grain, with result metrics and coherent representative rows. Heterogeneous grains still require explicit separate relations.
query_table_requests.proposal: Allow a grouped result to return named measures such as calls, failures, rate, timed calls, duration and price coverage. Reuse common input projections and aggregate leaves when possible, preserving a coherent snapshot.
examples: Failure rate with numerator and denominator
query_table_requests.performance: An HTTP batch is not necessarily one scan. Preserve Pharos cube rewrites and weighted sums rather than rescanning raw calls for every small preview.
query_table_requests.current_status: V3 produces named summaries at one grain, with result metrics and coherent representative rows. Heterogeneous grains still require explicit separate relations.

query_table_requests.title: Scalar percentiles and explicit precision
query_table_requests.gap: Scalar MEDIAN and exact box quartiles execute in both the local core and Go profile. Arbitrary scalar percentiles such as p95 remain unavailable.
query_table_requests.proposal: Add typed median/percentile reductions usable in formulas and named measures, with shared TS/server conformance. Advertise exact or approximate algorithms, numeric sample count and precision.
query_table_requests.performance: Exact ordering can be expensive and existing sum/min/max cubes cannot reconstruct quantiles. Offer sketches only with explicit approximation semantics.
query_table_requests.current_status: Scalar MEDIAN and exact box quartiles execute in both the local core and Go profile. Arbitrary scalar percentiles such as p95 remain unavailable.

query_table_requests.proposal: Extend inspection with metric identity, typed group keys, selected range or mark and resolved query context. Provide a host resolver for contributing rows and bounded exemplar hydration; preserve source IDs and evidence locators.

The sessions inside an outlier bin

query_table_requests.gap: Standalone MetricCard and headless useAggregations are already exported. The chart is internally tied to card chrome and normal axis/legend sizing.

query_table_requests.performance: Rendering remains bounded by marks and labels and should never trigger a second computation for presentation-only edits.
query_table_requests.current_status: Home uses the exported native MetricCard in a bounded compact wrapper. This is a Pharos presentation adapter; a dedicated upstream plot-only contract remains proposed.

query_table_requests.title: Coverage freshness clocks and execution budgets
query_table_requests.gap: The v2 compiler and integration guide already specify shared clock/snapshot identity and host-owned response metadata. Pharos has not adopted the contract; freshness, moving-window cache expiry and source coverage need an end-to-end agreement.
query_table_requests.proposal: Adopt and finish the existing contract with final input/sample/group counts, truncation/precision, host data revision, echoed as-of clock and cache expiry for moving windows. Carry host-provided source freshness/coverage separately from computational exactness. Enforce deadlines/cancellation and explicit rejected plans.
examples: Fast reloads with fresh relative windows
query_table_requests.performance: Cache on data and definition revision plus resolved clock/window; LIMIT only bounds output. Host-level candidate scheduling should prioritize visible previews.
query_table_requests.current_status: V2 returns computational coverage, processed rows and group counts with explicit execution budgets/cancellation. Host data freshness, provenance and cross-request snapshot guarantees remain separate.

query_table_requests.title: Portable execution profiles and conformance fixtures
query_table_requests.gap: The new Go planner emits PostgreSQL casts/functions. Pharos runs SQLite and its own map executor; v2 is not available by changing frontend dependencies.
query_table_requests.proposal: Provide a dialect-neutral validated execution plan or a documented adapter seam plus portable semantic fixtures. Add a SQLite profile where appropriate, or let Pharos implement the same negotiated v2 contract without pretending every function is portable.
examples: All new all-matching formulas and distributions in Pharos
query_table_requests.performance: Retain SQLite indexes, FTS and cube routing. Hosts own actual execution, deadlines and prepared views; conformance checks cover nulls, errors, lazy branches and numeric precision.
query_table_requests.current_status: All ten schemas execute through the negotiated qt-sqlite-v1 profile, with canonical revisions, typed rows and integration/conformance coverage.

query_table_requests.title: An indexed search predicate seam
query_table_requests.gap: The host indexed message/Library search relation participates in V2/V3 counts and groups with explicit bounded-search coverage. A reusable upstream search seam remains a request.
query_table_requests.proposal: Let a host advertise a persisted, typed indexed-search predicate/source that participates in the same counts, groups and cache identity as ordinary filters. Define matched-row versus parent-membership semantics and bounded-search coverage; Pharos supplies FTS and excerpt hydration.
examples: Agent confusion in the last seven days
query_table_requests.performance: Apply role and message-time constraints to the match population. Do not replace indexed search with a regex scan of every transcript or filter workspace activity dates as if they were message dates.
query_table_requests.current_status: The host indexed message/Library search relation participates in V2/V3 counts and groups with explicit bounded-search coverage. A reusable upstream search seam remains a request.

query_table_requests.title: Grouped time series and heatmap presentation
query_table_requests.gap: Line charts are one chronological series; two-key output has a pivot/table route, but no explicit heatmap or shared stacked-series chart contract.
query_table_requests.proposal: Support time × category series with explicit missing/zero semantics, stacked or grouped marks, stable colors and an exact remainder; add a bounded two-key heatmap. Share full and compact renderers.
query_table_requests.performance: Bound time buckets and categories; preserve totals when folding an additive remainder. Do not smooth missing observations or sum rates across categories.
query_table_requests.current_status: Native line/bar series and pivots are available; Home retains calendar-aware Usage columns with shared colors. Native heatmaps and the full missing/zero/remainder series contract remain deferred.

query_table_requests.title: Bounded expansion of set-valued dimensions
query_table_requests.gap: Arrays support membership filtering but are not admitted server row expressions; grouping a host list is not grouping each member.
query_table_requests.proposal: Offer an explicit explode-members stage or a normalized host relation with declared parent identity. Define event-count versus membership-count measures and restrict simultaneous expansions to prevent accidental cross products.
examples: All files touched by a work
query_table_requests.performance: Index normalized members or materialize them during ingestion. Carry distinct parent IDs to avoid multiplying usage or costs across memberships.

query_table_requests.title: Editable bookmark metadata with stable IDs
query_table_requests.gap: SavedQuery carries name, timestamp and QueryState. StorageAdapter has saveNamed/delete, but no stable-ID update for name/description/order or discovery across dataset namespaces.
query_table_requests.proposal: Add optional stable-ID bookmark updates for title, description and user order, and a host-controlled way to enumerate relevant bookmarks across dataset namespaces. Keep queries as canonical storage and preserve existing adapters.
examples: Rename and describe a collected card
Keep one query identity across surfaces
query_table_requests.performance: This is storage/API work rather than metric computation. Metadata changes should not invalidate arithmetic or recreate saved IDs.
query_table_requests.current_status: Stable bookmark metadata, ordering and cross-dataset collection are host-owned. Optional coverMetricId selects a saved metric without changing the query or bookmark ID.

query_table_requests.title: Registered relationships with explicit cardinality
query_table_requests.gap: The host can already supply a joined SourceSQL, but users cannot compose registered dataset relationships.
query_table_requests.proposal: Consider approved relation joins or semi-joins with declared grain and cardinality, not arbitrary SQL. Provide fanout-aware measures and source lineage.
query_table_requests.performance: Prejoin recurring relationships in Pharos first; index join keys and prevent multiplication of already-aggregated facts.

query_table_requests.title: Ordered partition functions
query_table_requests.gap: Formula context rejects windows and source order is not exposed as an analytical operation.
query_table_requests.proposal: Consider LAG/LEAD, first/last-by-order, running counts and elapsed differences over a declared partition and stable event ordering.
query_table_requests.performance: Use partition/order indexes and bound the queried streams. Filter-after-window semantics may require earlier events outside a visible time window.

query_table_requests.title: Sessionization and event episode or funnel recipes
query_table_requests.gap: Recovery and verification episodes do not exist as generic metric inputs.
query_table_requests.proposal: Consider deterministic, bounded sessionization and ordered-pattern extraction over typed events. Keep definitions explicit and let hosts supply materialized episode rows.
query_table_requests.performance: Repeated homepage requests should query episode facts updated on ingestion rather than recompute every transcript sequence. Episode-boundary definitions are often domain-specific.

query_table_requests.title: Interval union overlap and concurrency
query_table_requests.gap: SUM(duration) cannot compute wall time for parallel activity; no interval transform is exposed.
query_table_requests.proposal: Consider typed interval-union length, overlap episodes and time-bucket occupancy as optional reducers or prepared host facts.
query_table_requests.performance: Sweep ordered interval endpoints rather than join every interval pair. Report open/missing endpoints and never substitute summed durations for elapsed time.

query_table_requests.title: Co-occurrence and association over prepared sets
query_table_requests.gap: File pairs and workflow motifs require pair/sequence creation and normalized marginal counts.
query_table_requests.proposal: Consider bounded association reducers over prepared membership or edge datasets: support count, joint frequency and explicit marginals for lift. Keep pair generation and semantic labels in the host initially.
query_table_requests.performance: Pair expansion can be quadratic; cap set size, use incremental sparse counts and minimum support before ranking.

query_table_requests.title: Named scenario parameters and aligned variants
query_table_requests.gap: Literal arithmetic can already calculate a scenario once rates and inputs are fields, but no reusable parameter bundle or named variant output exists.
query_table_requests.proposal: Consider typed saved parameters with units and several labeled variants over the same prepared population. Hosts supply rates and billing data.
query_table_requests.performance: Reuse workload projections across scenarios. Keep parameters out of display labels and external lookups out of expression execution.

query_table_requests.title: An optional result renderer registration seam
query_table_requests.gap: Current chart families do not render transcript excerpts, event paths, parallel lanes or trees.
query_table_requests.proposal: Consider host-rendered result kinds with typed validated payloads, inspect callbacks, theme access and compact/full variants. Avoid building every domain-specific cover into the core library.
query_table_requests.performance: Bound nodes/edges/excerpts, preserve query identity and defer hydration. Keep nonserializable callbacks out of saved-query state.

query_table_requests.title: A batch scheduler for heterogeneous previews
query_table_requests.gap: A v2 metric batch shares one WHERE, while a carousel pool spans filters, windows and datasets.
query_table_requests.proposal: Consider a reusable headless runner for several query plans with concurrency caps, cancellation, partial completion, memoization and visible-first priorities; the host may implement this without changing QueryState.
examples: Eligibility checks for a large suggestion pool
query_table_requests.performance: Group compatible candidates to share work, cache on explicit revisions/window anchors and fetch only a selected preview subset. Backend scan fusion is distinct from HTTP request batching.
query_table_requests.current_status: The headless preview runner batches compatible populations, caps metric batches at 20 and executions at three, publishes partial completion, isolates rejected formulas and supports cancellation and one-minute result reuse.

query_table_requests.title: Semantic interpretation inside metric expressions
query_table_requests.gap: Confusion loops, decisions, examples and scope changes require meaning extraction.
query_table_requests.proposal: Keep semantic extraction, embedding similarity and evidence-backed labels in Pharos. Query Table should consume their versioned annotations and indexed similarity result rows.
query_table_requests.performance: Do expensive extraction incrementally outside interactive queries; expose provenance and uncertain classifications.

query_table_requests.title: Automatic causal or quality judgments
query_table_requests.gap: Recorded outcomes and correlations cannot establish model superiority, productivity or cause.
query_table_requests.proposal: Offer explicit cohorts, denominators and underlying evidence. Keep domain scoring and recommendation ranking outside generic arithmetic; avoid a universal opaque success score.
query_table_requests.performance: Matched populations and statistical uncertainty are host/domain work; charting cannot solve confounding.

query_table_requests.title: Arbitrary SQL or recursive graph analytics in saved metrics
query_table_requests.gap: These would widen a deliberately allowlisted expression API into a general database language.
query_table_requests.proposal: Prefer registered sources, narrow relational stages and host-produced lineage closures or episode facts. Do not add raw user SQL, arbitrary recursive queries or unrestricted transcript regex as a homepage shortcut.
query_table_requests.performance: Unbounded graph/pair/text scans are poor interactive workloads and require host access and resource boundaries.

query_table_requests.title: Provider pricing billing or carbon models owned by Query Table
query_table_requests.gap: These require domain rate tables, assumptions and sometimes external/user data.
query_table_requests.proposal: Keep price books, billing inputs and energy models in Pharos. Query Table handles typed arithmetic, variants and visualization over prepared fields.
query_table_requests.performance: Version inputs and materialize compatible pricing components. Do not fetch providers as metric side effects.

query_table_requests.title: Automatically create database indexes or materializations for every saved formula
query_table_requests.gap: Expression execution does not imply a good database index, and definitions can change.
query_table_requests.proposal: Let the host measure plans and opt into projections, generated values, sketches or expression indexes. A core plan/explain hook is reasonable; automatic schema writes are not the default.
query_table_requests.performance: Account for ingestion/write cost, data volume and definition revisions; avoid proliferating expensive indexes for speculative cards.

capacity_audit.scope: All existing schema fields, SQL bindings, aggregate capabilities and retained data adapters reviewed. Narrow observed variants keep the original intended concept and its remaining evidence requirements.

human_word_review.denominators: Example/context percentages use assessed human contributions, including context-only messages. Workspace comparisons use contributions in each mapped repository/directory; no attribution to code changes is inferred.
